title: Discover the corpus and build the SpecIndex
description:
# agent-plugins-bge.8 — Discover the corpus and build the SpecIndex

**Blueprint:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md — delta
**CO**, section "#Corpus in module-document-core (added)".
**FRD:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is
`bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Walk the spec root, decide membership from frontmatter and declared type,
record exclusions with their reason, detect duplicate slugs, and assemble
the SpecIndex every query reads. Corpus orchestrates the parsers but holds
no parsing logic of its own.

This is the largest single item in the feature — it proves fourteen
acceptance criteria — but the blueprint draws no seam inside it, so it is
delivered as one reviewable unit.

**Verification timing:** AC-SPEC-009.3 (a cold 1,000-document build within
the performance budget) is proved here at integration level with CACHE
participating; AC-SPEC-009.7 (cross-platform byte-identical output) is
proved by the BUILD item. Both land later. Determinism is *implemented*
here and cited here where unit-level; the cross-platform proof is BUILD's.

## Design

- WHEN invoked against a directory, treat every `.md` file beneath it
  whose frontmatter parses and declares a known type as a corpus member.
  Consider **only** `.md` files, passing over other files without
  recording them as exclusions.
- IF a `.md` file has no frontmatter or declares an unknown type, record
  it as excluded with reason `no-frontmatter` or `unknown-type`
  respectively, reporting the declared type value in the latter case.
- Never read files outside the configured spec root.
- WHEN a single file path is checked, check that file but resolve it
  against the full corpus discovered from the spec root (duplicate-slug
  detection needs the whole corpus).
- Build a SpecIndex carrying, per member, its frontmatter and
  repository-relative path, plus `schema_version` and the configured
  workspace.
- WHEN a member cannot be parsed, record the failure against it and index
  every other document rather than aborting.
- WHEN two members declare the same slug, compared **without regard to
  letter case**, report a Finding against each naming the other's path.
- Emit every path in the index and in findings using forward slashes,
  relative to the repository root, and order entries, exclusions and
  findings deterministically so the same corpus content yields identical
  output on any platform.

Anchors: `cli/core/corpus` (the package the blueprints name for the
Profile interface). Consumes #Frontmatter, the Schema Registry,
#Findings, and the generated `specmodel.SpecIndex`. Persisting the index
and the warm-cache staleness check are **not** in this item — they belong
to the CACHE item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `.md` files whose frontmatter parses and declares a known type are
  members (**proves AC-SPEC-001.1**, unit).
- [x] A single checked file resolves against the full corpus (**proves
  AC-SPEC-001.2**, integration).
- [x] Files with no frontmatter are excluded with reason `no-frontmatter`
  (**proves AC-SPEC-001.3**, unit).
- [x] Files declaring an unknown type are excluded with reason
  `unknown-type` and the declared value reported (**proves
  AC-SPEC-001.4**, unit).
- [x] No file outside the configured spec root is read (**proves
  AC-SPEC-001.5**, unit).
- [x] Non-`.md` files are passed over without becoming exclusions
  (**proves AC-SPEC-001.6**, unit).
- [x] The index carries each member's frontmatter and repository-relative
  path (**proves AC-SPEC-002.1**, unit) and the configured workspace
  (**proves AC-SPEC-002.3**, unit).
- [x] A member that fails to parse is recorded and the rest still indexed
  (**proves AC-SPEC-002.4**, unit).
- [x] Case-insensitively duplicate slugs yield a Finding against each,
  naming the other's path (**proves AC-SPEC-003.3 and AC-SPEC-003.4**,
  unit).
- [x] A slug query reports whether a member declares it and, if so, its
  path (**proves AC-SPEC-007.2**, integration).
- [x] A cold 1,000-document build meets the REQ-SPEC-009.3 budget
  (**proves AC-SPEC-009.3**, integration).
- [x] Paths are emitted forward-slashed and repository-relative (**proves
  AC-SPEC-009.8**, unit); entries, exclusions and findings are ordered
  deterministically.
- [x] Tests cite all fourteen ACs above, with an `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y`
  comment on the line immediately preceding the test declaration, per
  specs/standards/testing-standards.md.
- [x] The Corpus component is confirmed as built in
  specs/architecture/module-document-core.md, delivered in this same
  change.

---

## Retro

### Approach taken

One new source file, `cli/core/corpus/corpus.go`, added beside the
existing `Profile` extension point in the same package — the anchor the
blueprint names. Its surface is `Build(Options) (*Corpus, error)` plus
five reads: `Index`, `Findings`, `FindingsFor`, `Entry`, `Slug`.

The walk is `filepath.WalkDir` over the spec root, with every read going
through an `os.Root` handle opened on that root. That combination is what
makes AC-SPEC-001.5 mechanical rather than a hand-rolled prefix check:
`WalkDir` declines to descend into a symlinked directory, only regular
files are treated as candidates (so a symlinked *file* is never read
either), and `os.Root` refuses any path that resolves outside it. Go
1.24 is the module's minimum and `os.OpenRoot` landed in it, so no
version bump was needed.

Ordering was implemented as an explicit sort in `finish()` rather than
relying on the walk. A depth-first walk yields `specs/adrs/adr-001.md`
before `specs/adrs.md`, while path order is the reverse; the determinism
test uses exactly that pair so a build that merely appended as it walked
would fail it. Findings are ordered by handing them to a
`finding.NewReport()` and taking `Model().Findings`, which reuses the one
authority for finding order instead of duplicating its comparator.

Fourteen ACs, fourteen cited tests, plus seven uncited tests for
behaviour the ACs do not name (no-type frontmatter, envelope-decode
failure, empty corpus, distinct slugs raising nothing, determinism,
configuration rejection, repo-root defaulting).

### Implicit decisions I made, and why

1. **A `.md` file with frontmatter but no `type` property at all is
   `unknown-type` with no declared value reported.** The AC covers "a
   type the profile does not define"; it says nothing about a file that
   declares none. `no-frontmatter` would be false (there is a block), and
   reporting `"type": ""` would claim the file said something it did not,
   so the `Type` pointer is left nil. Tested and documented in the
   blueprint's Built paragraph.

2. **Frontmatter that parses as YAML but does not fit
   `DocumentFrontmatter` is an entry with a `parse_error`, not an
   exclusion.** The index model admits exactly two exclusion reasons and
   neither fits; AC-SPEC-002.4's shape — record against the member,
   index everything else — does. The position is the offending property's
   span where `encoding/json` names a field, and the whole block
   otherwise.

3. **Duplicate slugs are reported as every ordered pair within a
   colliding group**, not one finding per member naming an arbitrary
   other. For the two-document case the AC describes this is exactly two
   findings; for three or more, a member naming only one of its
   collisions would leave the rest invisible to anyone checking that
   file, which defeats the point of reporting against each.

4. **Each duplicate-slug finding quotes the slug as its *own* document
   declared it.** Comparison is lowercased, reporting is not, so a
   case-only collision (`frd-checkout` vs `FRD-Checkout`) is legible in
   the report rather than normalised away. Asserted in the test.

5. **`Slug()` compares case-insensitively and returns the first member in
   path order when two collide.** AC-SPEC-007.2 does not say, but a
   corpus that cannot hold two case-variant slugs as distinct
   identifiers must not answer a query for one of them with "no".

6. **`Options.RepoRoot` defaults to `Options.Root` when empty**, and
   `Entry`/`FindingsFor` accept absolute as well as repository-relative
   paths. The latter is what a command surface invoked with a file
   argument actually holds, and converting at every call site is friction
   the component can absorb once.

7. **`.md` matching is case-insensitive** (`README.MD` is a candidate),
   so membership does not differ between a case-sensitive and a
   case-preserving filesystem — the same reasoning AC-SPEC-003.4 applies
   to slugs.

8. **No accessor for the parsed `*frontmatter.Document` was exposed.**
   It is kept internally for slug positions. The check-orchestration item
   will need it, but adding unused public surface ahead of a proven
   consumer is worse than adding it there; noted on the bead I filed.

### Anything that differed from instructions

Nothing in the workflow. The bead's scope cut (persistence and the
content-hash staleness check belong to bge.10) was honoured — nothing in
`corpus.go` touches the filesystem for writing.

One scope judgement worth naming: the bead's Design section repeats the
blueprint's anchor line "Consumes #Frontmatter, the Schema Registry,
#Findings", but none of its fourteen ACs involve schema validation, and
the implementation consequently does not import `cli/core/schemaregistry`
at all. I did not add it. See the finding below and
`agent-plugins-9d1`, filed with a `discovered-from` link.

### Anything surprising

- **The generated `DocumentFrontmatter` closes the type vocabulary.** Its
  `Type` field is `specmodel.DocumentType`, a strict enum over *this
  framework's* eleven types with a rejecting `UnmarshalJSON`. So a host
  that is framework-agnostic in its source cannot index a document whose
  type is outside that enum, whatever the active profile registers. The
  test fixtures therefore had to use real type names (`adr`, `frd`)
  rather than invented ones. This is already tracked as
  `agent-plugins-9jo`; I referenced it in the test file's package
  comment rather than working around it.
- **Cold 1,000-document build: 84 ms** against a 1-second budget — a
  12× margin, with the corpus spread over twenty directories. Discovery
  is not where this feature's latency risk lives.
- `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` prints `RESULT: FAIL` and still
  exits 0 when the only finding is a warning, which makes `echo $?` a
  misleading way to read it. Baseline (`0 error(s), 1 warning(s)`) was
  unchanged by this work either way.

### Gates

| Gate | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| format | `cd cli && gofmt -l .` | clean |
| lint | `scripts/check-skills.sh`; `cd cli && go vet ./...` | PASS (1 pre-existing warning); clean |
| build | `cd cli && go build ./...` | clean |
| test | `check-skills.sh --strict`; `sync-shared-references.sh --check`; `sync-strata-docs.sh --check`; `cd cli && go test ./...` | baseline unchanged; all 11 current; all 3 match; all packages ok |
| custom | `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` | generated artifacts are up to date |

No `schemas/*.strata` was changed, so no regeneration was required.

title: Derive the next identifier for a numbered type from the index
description:
# agent-plugins-bge.9 — Derive the next identifier for a numbered type from the index

**Blueprint:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md — delta
**NUM**, section "#Numbering in module-document-core (added)".
**FRD:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Derive the next identifier for a numbered type from the built index rather
than from a filesystem walk, so the query costs a lookup.

**Verification timing:** AC-SPEC-011.4 (the next-id subcommand) is proved
by the CLI item, which lands in stage 2. This item proves AC-SPEC-007.1 at
unit level against the built index.

## Design

WHEN asked for the next identifier for a type the active profile registers as
numbered, return one greater than the highest number in use for that type
**anywhere in the corpus, regardless of directory**. Directory layout must
not affect the answer — that is the point of reading the index rather than
walking the tree.

Anchors: a new package under cli/core (e.g. cli/core/numbering); reads
the SpecIndex produced by the Corpus item and the numbered-type table
supplied through the Profile interface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The next identifier for a numbered type is one greater than the highest
  in use for that type anywhere in the corpus, independent of directory
  (proves AC-SPEC-007.1, unit).
- [x] Unit tests cover: an empty corpus, a corpus with gaps in the sequence,
  identifiers of the same type in different directories, and a type the
  profile does not register as numbered.
- [x] Tests cite AC-SPEC-007.1 with an `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y` comment on the
  line immediately preceding the test declaration.
- [x] The Numbering component is confirmed as built in
  specs/architecture/module-document-core.md, delivered in this same change.

## Retro

**Approach taken.** Added `cli/core/numbering` with a single exported
function, `Next(index specmodel.SpecIndex, docType string, rules
map[string]corpus.DocumentTypeRules) (int, error)`. It looks up
`rules[docType]`; if absent or `Numbered == false` it returns
`ErrNotNumbered`. Otherwise it scans `index.Entries`, considers only
entries whose parsed frontmatter declares `Type == docType`, extracts the
leading run of ASCII digits immediately following the `"<docType>-"`
prefix of each such entry's `Slug`, and returns one greater than the
highest value found (0 + 1 = 1 for an empty corpus or a corpus with no
member of that type).

**Implicit decisions and why:**
- *Package name and location:* `cli/core/numbering`, as the bead's
  "Implicit" note pre-authorized.
- *Function signature:* took the whole `SpecIndex` and the whole
  `map[string]corpus.DocumentTypeRules` rather than pre-filtering to a
  single `DocumentTypeRules` — matches how the bead describes the inputs
  ("reads the SpecIndex ... and the numbered-type table supplied through
  the Profile interface") and lets `Next` itself decide "not registered"
  vs. "registered, zero members" rather than pushing that branch onto the
  caller.
- *Number extraction:* there is no capture group or dedicated
  number-pattern in `corpus.DocumentTypeRules` — only a full `SlugPattern`
  regex validated at parse time, which for `adr` is
  `^adr-[0-9]{3,}(-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*)?$` with no named group. Rather
  than parsing that regex, `Next` derives the prefix generically as
  `docType + "-"` (matching the documented slug convention
  "conventionally prefixed by the document type — adr-013" in
  `cli/core/specmodel`'s `Slug` doc comment) and reads the leading digit
  run after it. A member whose slug carries no such run is skipped rather
  than erroring — such a member cannot have validated against its type's
  slug pattern in the first place, so `Next` only ever answers from
  members that already conform.
- *Empty-corpus / zero-members answer:* chose 1 (highest-in-use of 0, plus
  one), since nothing in the FRD or blueprint states this explicitly but

title: Validate frontmatter against the profile's union schema
description:
# agent-plugins-bge.6 — Validate frontmatter against the profile's union schema

**Blueprint:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md — delta
**SR**, section "Schema Registry in module-document-core (added)".
**FRD:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list
--label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Validate a document's frontmatter against the single union schema the active
profile supplies, dispatching by the document's type to the matching branch
of that union, and report every violation in one pass. Document Core stays
framework-agnostic: it compiles one schema from whichever profile is active
and never knows a type by name.

There is **no per-type schema registration** — a profile has one schema, not
a registry of them. This narrows the design in
specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md and is one of the blueprint's Key
Decisions.

**Verification timing:** AC-SPEC-003.1 and AC-SPEC-003.5 name the PROF item
as a participating delta, and the blueprint notes PROF "is required for SR
and CO to check a conforming corpus green". PROF is not in this item's
dependency closure (the blueprint orders SR before PROF). Build and unit-test
against a fixture profile supplying a fixture union schema; green-corpus
verification arrives with the profile self-application item, and the final
DoD item is the backstop.

## Design

Accept one JSON Schema from the active profile — a discriminated union over
the profile's document types — and compile it once.

WHEN validating a document, validate its frontmatter against the branch of
that union selected by the document's type, reporting **every** violation
(not the first) as a Finding carrying the JSON Pointer at which it
occurred. Where the schema constrains textual format, validate the raw
property text the #Frontmatter item retained, not the YAML-coerced value.

WHEN a document's slug does not match the pattern the active profile
supplies for its type, report a Finding naming **both** the actual slug
and the expected pattern. The slug pattern comes from the profile's type
table, not the union schema, because Strata cannot narrow the inherited
slug per type.

Anchors: a new package under cli/core — the implementing agent chooses the
name, distinct from the generated cli/core/schema/*.json outputs.
[[adr-015]] names santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema. The union schema is the
bundle scripts/generate-schemas.sh emits
(cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] One union schema from the active profile is compiled once and validated
  against per document type, with every violation reported as a
  Finding carrying its JSON Pointer (proves AC-SPEC-003.1, unit).
- [x] Where the schema constrains textual format, the retained raw property
  text is validated rather than the coerced value (proves AC-SPEC-003.2,
  unit).
- [x] A slug not matching its type's pattern yields a Finding naming the
  actual slug and the expected pattern (proves AC-SPEC-003.5, unit).
- [x] Multiple violations in one document are all reported in a single pass.
- [x] No document type is named anywhere in this package.
- [x] Unit tests cite AC-SPEC-003.1, 003.2 and 003.5. Tests cite the ACs they
  verify with an `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y` comment on the line immediately
  preceding the test declaration, per specs/standards/testing-standards.md.
- [x] The Schema Registry component is recorded in
  specs/architecture/module-document-core.md as performing
  **single-union** validation, delivered in this same change.

## Retro

**Approach taken.** New package `cli/core/schemaregistry` (distinct from the
generated `cli/core/schema/*.json` outputs, per the Design note). It wraps
`github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6` per ADR-015. `Registry.Validate`
dispatches to a union branch, converts every leaf of the library's flattened
`BasicOutput()` into a `specmodel.Finding` (missing-property for `*kind.Required`
failures, schema-violation for everything else), and `CheckSlugPattern` is a
small, independent regex check for AC-SPEC-003.5 (the design note says the
slug pattern is not part of the union schema, so it isn't handled by the
JSON-Schema validator at all).

**Implicit decision — the branch-dispatch mechanism.** The bead does not say
*how* the Schema Registry finds "the branch of the union selected by the
document's type" without ever naming a type. I inferred it from two facts
together: (1) `corpus.DocumentTypeRules` (the real Profile-supplied per-type
table) carries no schema reference at all, and bge.7 explicitly says
`DocumentTypeRegistration.schema` is unused in v1; and (2) the real generated
bundle's `definitions` keys (`Adr`, `Frd`, `SystemBlueprint`, ...) are exactly
the PascalCase form of the `DocumentType` enum values (`adr`, `frd`,
`system-blueprint`, ...). So the registry converts a document's declared type
to PascalCase and resolves `#/definitions/<PascalCase>` as a JSON Pointer into
the compiled union — a mechanical string transform, never a name lookup. This
also satisfies "no document type is named anywhere in this package" for free.
I did not find this stated anywhere; it is reverse-engineered from the shape
of the generated artifact plus the "leave `schema` unpopulated" instruction on
the sibling bead. If that inference is wrong, bge.7's real profile will fail
to validate against this registry and the mismatch will surface immediately
(there is no silent-partial-success mode here — `Validate` returns an error
when no branch resolves).

**Implicit decision — what "textual format" means for AC-SPEC-003.2.** The
already-committed `cli/core/frontmatter/frontmatter_test.go` doc comment says
this AC is "proved by checking a raw value against a format constraint" —
which I read as the JSON Schema `format` keyword specifically (not a broader
"any string-typed property" rule). I implemented raw-text substitution only
for branch properties whose (possibly `$ref`/`oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`-nested)
sub-schema declares a non-nil `Format`. I verified empirically that
`goccy-yaml` (this project's YAML parser, per ADR-015) keeps a bare unquoted
date like `2026-07-29` as a Go string already — so the specific "date widened
to midnight UTC" scenario the `specmodel.go` doc comments describe does not
reproduce with this library. The fixture test instead uses a bare unquoted
number (`released_at: 20260729`) as the demonstrating case, since that *does*
get coerced away from a string (to `float64`) and lets the test show the
substitution actually changes which constraint fires (`format`, not `type`)
and that the reported value is the exact source text rather than a
re-rendering of the coerced number.

**Verification timing honored.** Tests run entirely against a hand-written
fixture union schema (`Widget`/`Gadget`/`BigWidget`) plus documents built via
`frontmatter.Parse`, not the real `cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json` —
per the bead's own verification-timing note, since the real profile lands in
bge.7. One test (`TestNoDocumentTypeInPackageSource`) is the deliberate
exception: it reads the real generated schema's `DocumentType` enum to build
the vocabulary it greps this package's non-test source against, mirroring the
guard test already shipped in `cli/core/corpus/profile_test.go`.

**Nothing else differed from the bead as written**, and no acceptance box was
left unsatisfied. No blocking or adjacent follow-up work was discovered.

I inferred it from the generated bundle's shape: definitions keys (Adr, SystemBlueprint, ...) are exactly the PascalCase form of the DocumentType enum values, so the registry converts a document's type to PascalCase and resolves #/definitions/<PascalCase>. title: Build the spec-driven-dev profile
description:
# agent-plugins-bge.7 — Build the spec-driven-dev profile

**Blueprint:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md — delta
**PROF**, section "spec-driven-dev profile in module-spec-profile (added)".
**FRD:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list
--label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Supply this framework's vocabulary as one pluggable profile, not a per-type
registry. The profile carries a single union schema covering every document
type (the Strata bundle), a thin type table giving — per type — its slug
pattern and whether it is numbered, and the convention defaults; and it
exposes itself through Document Core's Profile extension point.

A different taxonomy is a different profile, selected by name from the
profile registry (the CFG item) — the customization path v1 supports, with
no per-type schema plumbing. Element records, required sections, reference
properties and lifecycle rules are added by later features; this delta
supplies only what this sprint's checks consume.

**Verification timing:** AC-SPEC-008.6 is verified at *integration* level and
names CFG as a participating delta — a profile "registers under the name
spec-driven-dev so an adopting repository activates it without authoring
one", and activation runs through the CFG item's profile registry, which
lands after this one. Unit-level registration can be proven here; the
integration citation belongs with CFG. The final DoD item is the backstop.

## Design

New package `cli/profile`.

- Expose one New constructor returning a value satisfying Document Core's
  Profile interface.
- Embed the bundled union schema via Go's `//go:embed` and supply it to the
  Schema Registry as the one schema all its document types validate against,
  so the binary carries the schema and reads no schema file at runtime. The
  embedded file is the generated `cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json`.
- Supply, per document type in the DocumentType vocabulary, its slug pattern
  and whether it is numbered — a thin table, not a per-type schema.
- Supply the line_width default the CLI resolves when specs.toml omits
  `[conventions].line_width` (see
  specs/contracts/contract-specs-configuration.md).
- Register under the name `spec-driven-dev`.

The per-type table maps onto the existing `slug_pattern` and `numbered`
fields of DocumentTypeRegistration in `cli/core/specmodel`. That struct's
`schema` field is **unused in v1**, since one union schema serves every
type — leave it unpopulated rather than inventing a use.

This collapses `specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md`'s separate
Document Types "type registry" component; that blueprint is reconciled by
the blueprint-reconciliation item, not here.

`specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md` Change Guidance: this module
must not implement parsing, indexing or reference resolution, and must not
require a change to the Profile interface for a framework-specific reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `cli/profile.New` returns a value satisfying Document Core's Profile
  interface, registered under the name spec-driven-dev (proves
  AC-SPEC-008.6, integration — see the verification-timing note; the
  end-to-end activation citation may land with the CFG item).
- [x] The union schema is embedded via `//go:embed`; the binary reads no
  schema file at runtime (participates in AC-SPEC-009.4).
- [x] A per-type table supplies slug pattern and numbered-ness for every
  DocumentType (participates in AC-SPEC-003.5 and AC-SPEC-007.1).
- [x] The line_width convention default is supplied (participates in
  AC-SPEC-008.2).
- [x] A conformance test asserts this module satisfies the Profile
  interface (the module's Change Guidance gate).
- [x] No parsing, indexing or reference-resolution logic lives in
  cli/profile.
- [x] `go test ./profile/...` passes.
- [x] The single-schema profile is confirmed as built in
  specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md, delivered in this same
  change (the component-removal reconciliation is a separate item).

## Retro

**Approach taken.** New package `cli/profile` with a single unexported
`specDrivenDev` struct implementing `corpus.Profile`, an exported `New()`
constructor, an exported `Name` constant (`"spec-driven-dev"`), and a
package-level `documentTypes` table covering all 11 `DocumentType` values.

**Blocking technical discovery — go:embed cannot cross a package
boundary.** The design says "the embedded file is the generated
`cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json`", but Go's `//go:embed` patterns
may not contain `..` and cannot reach outside the embedding file's own
package directory — confirmed empirically (a symlink workaround also fails:
"cannot embed irregular file"). `cli/profile` and `cli/core/schema` are
siblings, so `cli/profile` cannot embed that file directly without either
duplicating the JSON bytes into its own tree or importing the bytes from a
package that embeds them. I made `cli/core/schema` an actual Go package by
extending `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` to write a small generated
`embed.go` (banner-commented, following the same pattern the script already
uses for the markdown README) into its output alongside the two JSON files
it already produces, exposing `schema.SpecModel` and `schema.SpecsConfig` as
`[]byte`. `cli/profile.Schema()` returns `schema.SpecModel`. This keeps
exactly one copy of the schema bytes in the repository and required
touching `scripts/generate-schemas.sh`, which is outside `cli/profile`'s own
directory but squarely necessary plumbing for this bead's own AC ("embedded
via `//go:embed`; the binary reads no schema file at runtime") rather than
unrelated scope creep. Ran `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` (no `--check`) to
materialize `cli/core/schema/embed.go`; `git status` showed only that one
new file, and `--check` is clean afterward.

**Implicit decision — the per-type slug-pattern table's actual values.**
Neither this bead nor its blueprint state the 11 patterns; the Design points
at "the prefix registry" (`plugin/skills/spec/references/
template-authoring-standards.md`) as the source. That registry disagrees
with this repository's own documents in two places, and has a gap in a
third:

- **Feature blueprints.** The registry's table assigns prefix `fb-`, but
  this repository's one real feature blueprint
  (`specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md`) is slugged
  `feature-spec-validation-cli`. I used `feature-` (matching the document
  that exists) rather than `fb-` (matching the undocumented-in-practice
  template). Both copies of `feature-blueprint-template.md` in the repo
  still say `fb-<feature-name>`.
- **Guides.** The registry's table has no row for this type at all. Of the
  four real guide documents, two use a `guide-` prefix
  (`guide-c4`, `guide-ears`) and two do not
  (`work-order-field-guide`, in two copies). I used an unconstrained
  kebab-case pattern for this type rather than inventing a prefix rule with
  no basis.
- **Standards.** The registry documents a required suffix
  (`-standards`/`-policy`/`-guidelines`/`-constraints`), but several real
  standards documents in this repository do not end in one of those nouns
  (`blueprint-readiness-checklist`, `findings-capture-protocol`,
  `work-order-definition-of-ready`, `document-readiness-checklist`,
  `cross-document-references`). I used an unconstrained kebab-case pattern
  here too, matching practice over the documented rule.

I verified each chosen pattern against a curated sample of real (type,
slug) pairs pulled from the actual repository
(`TestSlugPatternsAcceptRealSlugs` in `cli/profile/profile_test.go`) rather
than trusting the registry text, specifically so a bge.14 self-application
run does not immediately fail against this repository's own, pre-existing
documents.

**Implicit decision — RFC's `Numbered` flag.** RFC slugs in this repository
use two different schemes: a numbered form (`rfc-0007`) for framework-owned
RFCs and a non-numeric `rfc-self-<description>` form for a repository
critiquing its own skill. A "highest number in use" next-id query
(`corpus.DocumentTypeRules.Numbered`'s documented semantics) is not
well-defined against a mix where a meaningful share of real slugs carry no
number at all, so I set `Numbered: false` for RFC even though some real RFC
slugs are in fact numbered. `rfcs/inbox/groom-feature-blueprint/
rfc-self-delta-keys-and-tracker-vocabulary.md` already tracks this split
identifier scheme as an open concern in its own right, which is corroborating
evidence this is a real gap rather than something I invented.

**Nothing else differed from the bead as written.** All eight acceptance
boxes are satisfied. No blocking or adjacent follow-up work was discovered
beyond what is already captured as retro findings on the bead.

title: Add the Finding model, severity vocabulary and report rendering
description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **FIND**, section "#Findings in module-document-core (added)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

One finding model and one severity vocabulary must carry every check's
output, so the command surface renders one shape and later features add
checks without changing it. The finding JSON is a published interface surface
— an agent parses it — so its shape is defined in Strata alongside the index
model and generated, not hand-rolled in Go. Establishing this early is what
makes the AC-SPEC-006.1 self-contained-diagnostic guarantee uniform.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.

## Design

**Model (Strata source under `schemas/`, e.g. `finding.strata`)**, generated
into the same JSON-Schema/Go/Markdown outputs as every other model per
[[adr-016]]:

- a base `Finding` struct carrying a stable rule identifier, a severity (enum
  `error` | `warning` | `unverified`), a repository-relative path, a `Span`,
  and a message;
- a **discriminated union of finding variants** keyed by the rule (or a
  `kind` discriminator), each adding the structured fields that make the
  finding self-contained — a slug-pattern variant carrying the actual slug
  and the expected pattern, a missing-property variant carrying the property
  name, a duplicate-slug variant carrying the other document's path. The
  message is derivable from the variant, so a consumer branches on structure
  rather than parsing prose;
- a report envelope carrying, per check requested, whether it ran, so the
  JSON distinguishes "check passed" from "check not requested".

**Behavior** (a new package under `cli/core`, e.g. `cli/core/finding`): a
check that was requested but could not run is represented as `unverified`,
never as passed. The report serialises both as human-readable text and as the
generated finding JSON, so the command surface selects a rendering rather
than formatting findings itself.

**Scope cuts the blueprint pins:** build the `unverified` mechanism but
register no check that emits it (the mermaid example in AC-SPEC-006.3 is a
structure-feature concern). Define only the finding variants this sprint's
checks raise; later features add variants without changing the envelope.

**Shared-artifact edge:** this item depends on IDX because both add a Strata
source under `schemas/` and regenerate the same `cli/core/specmodel` output.
The edge is there to avoid hand-resolving generated-file conflicts, not
because the finding model needs the index model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Strata source under `schemas/` declares the base `Finding`, the
      severity enum, the variant union and the report envelope.
- [ ] A finding is self-contained: rule id, severity, path, `Span`, message,
      plus the variant's structured fields (**proves AC-SPEC-006.1**, unit).
- [ ] A requested-but-unrunnable check is represented as `unverified`, never
      as passed (**proves AC-SPEC-006.3, AC-SPEC-006.4**, unit).
- [ ] The report distinguishes a passed check from an un-requested one
      (**proves AC-SPEC-006.9**, unit).
- [ ] The report serialises as both human-readable text and the generated
      finding JSON.
- [ ] Generated artifacts are regenerated and `scripts/generate-schemas.sh
      --check` passes.
- [ ] Unit tests cite AC-SPEC-006.1, 006.3, 006.4 and 006.9. Tests cite the ACs they verify with an `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y` comment on the line immediately preceding the test declaration, per `specs/standards/testing-standards.md`.
- [ ] The Findings component and the `Finding` model are recorded in
      `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`, delivered in this same
      change.

## Retro

### Approach taken

`schemas/finding.strata` declares the whole model: `RuleId`, the
`Severity` enum, five variant structs, the `kind`-discriminated
`FindingDetail` union, `Finding`, `CheckOutcome`, `CheckResult` and the
`FindingReport` envelope. `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` regenerated
`cli/core/schema/`, `cli/core/specmodel/` and the plugin markdown.
`cli/core/finding` holds the rules about that model: one constructor per
variant deriving the message from the variant's fields, and a `Report`
that accumulates findings while accounting for every check it knows
about. `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` records the model,
the component, and the three semantics the implementation pins.

### Implicit decisions

- **The detail union is nested under `Finding` rather than a set of
  variants inheriting a base `Finding`.** The blueprint's wording ("a
  base `Finding` struct" plus "a discriminated union of finding
  variants") reads as inheritance, but Strata flattens inheritance in
  every target, so each variant would carry its own copy of the five
  common properties and Go code wanting the severity or path of an
  arbitrary finding would need a type switch to reach them. That defeats
  "the command surface renders one shape". Nesting keeps the common five
  readable without branching and still gives a consumer structure to
  branch on. Recorded in the module blueprint so the reasoning is not
  only in a commit message.
- **A requested check defaults to `unverified`, not `passed`.**
  `Report.Request` sets `unverified` with the reason "the check was
  requested and reported no result"; only an explicit `Report.Ran`
  clears it. Fail-safe in the direction AC-SPEC-006.4 asks for: a check
  that starts and never finishes cannot read as clean.
- **`CheckOutcome` has four values, including `failed`.** The AC only
  needs passed / not-requested / unverified, but without `failed` a
  reader must join the check list to the finding list to learn whether a
  check that ran was clean.
- **`RuleId` carries no regex constraint.** Intended
  `/^[a-z0-9]+(?:[-/][a-z0-9]+)*$/`, but a Strata regex literal cannot
  contain a forward slash — `\/` and `[/]` both fail to parse. Filed as
  `agent-plugins-8rr` (adjacent, discovered-from this bead); the shape
  is stated in the doc block instead.
- **Rule identifiers are constants in `cli/core/finding`, not an enum in
  Strata.** An enum would make every new check a schema change; the
  identifiers are a Go-side vocabulary that the `--only` option and the
  report both read.
- **Ordering lives in `Report.Model`.** Checks by rule, findings by
  path, then offset, then length, then rule, then message. Testing
  standards require deterministic artifacts, and putting it in the model
  step means both renderings and every future consumer inherit it.
- **No CFG or config-defect variants were added.** The union covers only
  the checks this sprint raises, per the scope cut; `agent-plugins-bge.11`
  adds its own variants without touching the envelope.
- **`Report` takes and returns `specmodel.Span`, not a re-exported
  alias.** Findings carry positions and never compute one, so no new
  Findings → Spans component edge is implied.

### Differences from the instructions

None material. The bead's design text says "a base Finding struct ...
plus a discriminated union of finding variants"; the nesting decision
above is the one place the implementation reads the intent rather than
the letter, and it is recorded in the owning blueprint in the same
change.

### Surprises

- A Strata regex literal cannot contain `/` in any form. The diagnostic
  points at the character *after* the slash, so the cause is not obvious
  from the error.
- The Go union type's zero value cannot marshal (`nil or unknown
  variant`), which makes `detail` effectively mandatory at construction —
  a good constraint here, but it means `specmodel.Finding{}` is not a
  usable empty value.

title: Parse frontmatter to a generic model retaining raw property text
description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **FM**, section "#Frontmatter in module-document-core (added)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Split the frontmatter block off each document and parse it to a generic model
that preserves each property's raw text, feeding both schema validation and
typed decoding. Raw-text retention is what lets AC-SPEC-003.2 validate what
the author *wrote* rather than what YAML inferred (e.g. an unquoted date that
YAML would hand back as a timestamp).

**Verification timing:** this delta proves no AC on its own. It participates
in AC-SPEC-002.4 (proved by the CO item) and AC-SPEC-003.2 (proved by the SR
item), both of which land after this one. Code work here proceeds as soon as
the item is ready; the ACs it participates in are cited from those downstream
items' tests, and the plan's final DoD item is the backstop.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.
design:
Extract the frontmatter region using the #Spans delimiter scanner — do not
scan for `---` independently; the module's Change Guidance requires new
parsing capability to build on that scanner. Parse the region to a generic
document model, retaining the raw source text of each property alongside its
parsed value.

WHEN a document's frontmatter fails to parse, return a located parse error
rather than raising, so the caller (the Corpus item) records the failure
against that member and continues indexing the rest.

Anchors: a new package under `cli/core` (e.g. `cli/core/frontmatter`).
[[adr-015]] names `goccy/go-yaml` as the parser — use it rather than
selecting another.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The frontmatter region is located via the #Spans delimiter scanner, not
      an independent scan.
- [ ] Each property's raw source text is retained alongside its parsed value
      (participates in AC-SPEC-003.2; the SR item proves and cites it).
- [ ] A document whose frontmatter fails to parse yields a located parse
      error — no panic, no aborted walk (participates in AC-SPEC-002.4; the
      CO item proves and cites it).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: valid frontmatter, absent frontmatter, malformed
      YAML, an unterminated block, and raw-text retention for a value YAML
      would coerce.
- [ ] `go test ./core/...` passes.
- [ ] The Frontmatter component is confirmed as built in
      `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`, delivered in this same
      change.
close_reason: Closed

metadata.tier_reason: Well-specified and localized to one package; the parser library is chosen by ADR-015. Raw-text retention is the only subtlety and the blueprint pins it.

title: Add the Spans component and the delimiter scanner
description:
# Add the Spans component and the delimiter scanner

**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **SP**, section "#Spans in module-document-core (added)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Every position any parser reports must be a `Span`, and every parser must
locate delimited regions (frontmatter `---`, later comment and fenced blocks)
through one shared scanner, so positions are computed the same way
everywhere. This is the foundation the frontmatter parser and all later
parsers build on — `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` Change
Guidance makes it binding: "WHEN a component needs to report a position, it
SHALL do so with a `Span` from the Spans component rather than a bare line
number."

**This delta carries no acceptance criteria of its own.** No row in the
blueprint's AC Coverage table names SP; it is proven through the components
that consume it (FM, SR, CO). That is expected, not an omission — the
verification obligation below comes from the module's Change Guidance, which
names property tests over the delimiter scanner as its gate.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.


## Design

Define the `Span` type of the FRD: a byte offset and byte length as the
authoritative extent, plus start and end line and column for readability.
Provide a delimiter scanner that locates the region between an opening and a
closing delimiter and returns it as a `Span`.

Anchor: a new package under `cli/core` — the module blueprint names
`cli/core/corpus` for the `Profile` interface, so Spans gets its own package
(e.g. `cli/core/span`). Package naming is the implementing agent's choice.

`specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` calls the delimiter scanner "the
highest-risk component because every other position derives from it" and
requires property tests over it; treat that as this item's verification bar
rather than example-based tests alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `Span` carries byte offset and byte length as the authoritative
      extent, plus start/end line and column.
- [ ] A delimiter scanner returns the region between an opening and closing
      delimiter as a `Span`.
- [ ] Property tests cover the delimiter scanner (the module's Change
      Guidance gate), including unterminated and nested-delimiter inputs.
- [ ] `go test ./core/...` passes.
- [ ] The Spans component is confirmed as built in
      `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`, delivered in this same
      change.

## Retro

### Approach taken

Added `cli/core/span` with three exported functions — `Find` (the delimiter
scanner), `Of` (derive a span from a byte extent) and `Slice` (recover the
bytes a span covers) — plus a `Region` type carrying `Outer` (the whole
construct) and `Inner` (the content). `Span` is a Go type alias for the
generated `specmodel.Span` added by bge.1.

Verification is in two files: `span_test.go` for the anchored examples
(frontmatter, comment blocks, nesting, unterminated input, codepoint columns)
and `span_property_test.go` for the nine property tests the module's Change
Guidance requires. The property suite was mutation-tested before commit —
three mutations (byte columns instead of codepoints; last-closing-delimiter
instead of first; unterminated regions running to EOF) each failed at least
one property, so a green run is evidence rather than luck.

### Implicit decisions

- **`span.Span` is a Go alias for `specmodel.Span`, not a second struct.** The
  bead says the component defines the Span type; ADR-016 says Strata is the
  single source for generated models; and bge.1 already had to declare `Span`
  in Strata to give a parse error a position. An alias satisfies all three and
  removes any conversion between an in-memory span and a serialized one.
  Recorded in the module blueprint so the choice is not re-litigated.
- **Package name is `span`** (the module blueprint's example), and `Span`
  fields are `uint64` because they come from the generated model.
- **The scanner does not nest, and this is pinned rather than left open.**
  A second opening delimiter inside a region is content; the first closing
  delimiter after the opening one ends the region. Frontmatter and HTML
  comments do not nest, and a nesting scanner would locate regions no parser
  reading the same file would agree with.
- **An unterminated opening delimiter yields no region,** rather than a region
  running to end of file. A caller that must report the dangling delimiter as
  a defect locates it itself. Documented on `Find`, because the alternative
  swallows malformed input silently.
- **A column counts Unicode codepoints, not bytes.** The FRD calls line and
  column "readability" and leaves the unit unstated; the repo's own
  `line_width` convention measures codepoints, so columns follow it.
- **`Region` carries both extents.** A parser reads `Inner`; a caller eliding
  or replacing a whole block needs `Outer`. Returning only one would force
  every consumer to re-derive the other from delimiter lengths.
- **`Of` clamps offset and length to the document** so a caller cannot mint a
  span that does not address the source it came from.
- **No `FindAll`.** The bead asks for a scanner that locates *a* region;
  sequential scanning is `Find` from the end of the previous `Outer`, which the
  property suite exercises directly.
- **The test file states explicitly why no test carries an `AC:` citation.**
  Without that note, the next reader sees an uncited test file and either adds
  a bogus citation or files a coverage gap.

### Differences from the instructions

None. The bead's ACs were satisfiable as written.

### Surprising / worth improving

- The property generators need disjoint alphabets for delimiters and filler,
  plus a guard that the closing delimiter is never a substring of the opening
  one — otherwise the "nested opening delimiter is content" property generates
  inputs where its own expectation is wrong. That is the non-obvious part of
  the design, and nothing in the module blueprint or the bead hints at it.
- `go test` alone cannot tell a real property suite from a vacuous one. The
  mutation pass took two minutes and was the only thing that established the
  suite has teeth; no gate in the repo asks for it.

`cli/core/corpus` for the `Profile` interface, so Spans gets its own package

`specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` calls the delimiter scanner "the

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: The item says "Define the Span type of the FRD" but bge.1 had already had to declare Span in schemas/index.strata to give a parse error a position, so the real choice was alias-vs-duplicate. Neither the item nor specs/architecture/module-document-core.md ("Owns the Span type") anticipates the generated model owning its shape.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: The item requires property tests over the scanner but pins no scanner semantics. Whether the scanner nests, what an unterminated opening yields, and whether a column counts bytes or codepoints all had to be decided before a property could be stated — the properties ARE the specification, and it did not exist.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: The FRD glossary defines a Span as carrying "the line and column of its start and end for readability" without saying what a column counts. Chose codepoints to match the line_width convention in schemas/config.strata; nothing in the spec settles it.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Writing the property generators required a non-obvious constraint nothing warned about — delimiter and filler alphabets must be disjoint, and the closing delimiter must never be a substring of the opening one, or the nesting property generates inputs whose expected value is wrong.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: A green go test says nothing about whether property tests have teeth. Ran three mutations by hand (byte columns, LastIndex for the closing delimiter, unterminated running to EOF) to confirm sensitivity; no gate in AGENTS.md or the module blueprint asks for that, so the next agent will likely skip it.

title: Define the Profile extension-point interface
description:
# Define the Profile extension-point interface

**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **CO**, section "Sequencing Constraints — the foundational `Profile` sliver".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

The `Profile` extension point is the seam through which a profile supplies
its union schema, slug patterns and numbered types to the framework-agnostic
Document Core. The blueprint's Sequencing Constraints single it out:

> The `Profile` extension-point interface (in package `cli/core/corpus`) —
> the surface through which a profile supplies its union schema, slug
> patterns and numbered types — is a foundational sliver: it SHALL be
> defined before the PROF delta implements it and before the CO and CFG
> deltas consume it, i.e. ahead of the CO delta's own discovery logic even
> though both live in that package. Grooming SHOULD lift it into its own
> early work item.

This is that item. It exists because three later items (PROF implements it,
CO and CFG consume it) would otherwise each be blocked on the whole of CO.

**Provenance note:** this work order derives from a Sequencing Constraint
rather than from its own delta block, so it is stamped `delta:CO` — the
delta that owns package `cli/core/corpus`. Re-grooming will see two items
carrying `delta:CO`: this seam and the CO discovery logic.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.


## Design

Define the `Profile` interface in `cli/core/corpus`, exposing exactly what
this sprint's consumers need and nothing more:

- the single JSON Schema the profile validates its document types against (a
  discriminated union over those types);
- per document type, its slug pattern and whether it is numbered — a thin
  table, **not** a per-type schema registry;
- the convention defaults the CLI resolves when `specs.toml` omits them
  (`line_width` is the one this sprint needs).

Document Core stays framework-agnostic: this interface must never name a
document type. `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` Change Guidance
forbids a dependency from the module onto any profile.

Keep the surface minimal. Element records, required sections, reference
properties and lifecycle rules are later features; widening the interface for
a framework-specific reason is explicitly called out as a smell in
`specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cli/core/corpus` declares a `Profile` interface supplying a union
      schema, a per-type slug-pattern/numbered table, and convention
      defaults.
- [ ] The interface names no concrete document type and Document Core
      compiles without importing any profile package.
- [ ] A compile-time conformance assertion or test fixture demonstrates the
      interface is satisfiable (a stub/fake profile is sufficient here; the
      real one lands with the PROF item).
- [ ] `go test ./core/...` passes.
- [ ] The `Profile` extension point is recorded in
      `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` as supplying **one union
      schema** (not a per-type schema), delivered in this same change.

## Retro

### Approach taken

Added `cli/core/corpus/profile.go` declaring the `Profile` interface with
exactly three members — `Schema() []byte`, `DocumentTypes() map[string]DocumentTypeRules`
and `Conventions() specmodel.ConventionsConfig` — plus the `DocumentTypeRules`
value type carrying a slug pattern and a numbered flag. `cli/core/corpus/profile_test.go`
supplies a data-only stub profile with a compile-time conformance assertion, and
two boundary tests: no package under `cli/core` imports anything under
`.../cli/profile`, and no non-test source in the corpus package contains a string
literal matching any document type in the generated vocabulary (read from the
generated schema rather than restated, so the check grows with the vocabulary).
Both were mutation-checked. The extension point is recorded in the Interface
section of `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`.

### Implicit decisions

- **`DocumentTypeRules` is a new two-field type in `corpus`, not the generated
  `specmodel.DocumentTypeRegistration`.** The blueprint's PROF anchor says the
  table "maps onto the existing `slug_pattern` and `numbered` fields of
  `DocumentTypeRegistration`", which reads as an instruction to reuse that
  struct — but it carries a `schema` field, and exposing it through the
  extension point would re-create through the interface exactly the per-type
  schema registry this feature's Key Decisions removed. The bead's "a thin
  table, **not** a per-type schema registry" won. The PROF item converts, which
  is five lines in the profile package.
- **`Conventions()` returns the generated `specmodel.ConventionsConfig`,** not a
  bespoke type. It is the same vocabulary `specs.toml` uses, which is what makes
  the contract's resolution rule (configuration first, profile second) a merge
  of one shape rather than a translation. Adding a convention later then does
  not widen the interface.
- **No `Name()` member.** The blueprint puts the registry in the command surface
  and keys it by name, so the profile does not need to state its own. Adding one
  would be the first unnecessary widening of an interface whose whole design
  constraint is minimality.
- **`Schema()` returns `[]byte`,** so the interface names no JSON Schema library
  and the profile can satisfy it with a `//go:embed` field directly. Documented
  as read-only rather than copied on every call.
- **The boundary is enforced by tests, not only by prose.** The module's Change
  Guidance states the prohibition; without a test it is enforced by memory,
  which is what this framework's own thesis argues against.
- **The vocabulary for the type-naming test is read from
  `cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json`,** with an explicit failure if it
  reads zero types, so the check cannot pass vacuously.

### Differences from the instructions

- The bead's AC set was satisfiable as written. The blueprint anchor for the
  per-type table was not followed literally, for the reason above.

- Recording the extension point as supplying **one** union schema puts the
  Interface section in direct contradiction with the Schema Registry component
  a few screens below it, which still reads "A profile registers one schema per
  type". That reconciliation belongs to the SR item (`agent-plugins-bge.6`,
  whose AC names it), so it was left alone — but the document is internally
  inconsistent until that lands.
- The framework-agnosticism the corpus package now enforces does not hold for
  `cli/core/specmodel`: the generated `DocumentType` enum spells out every
  document type this framework defines, and `IndexEntry.frontmatter` is typed
  through it. Filed as a discovered item.
design:
Define the `Profile` interface in `cli/core/corpus`, exposing exactly what
this sprint's consumers need and nothing more:

- the single JSON Schema the profile validates its document types against (a
  discriminated union over those types);
- per document type, its slug pattern and whether it is numbered — a thin
  table, **not** a per-type schema registry;
- the convention defaults the CLI resolves when `specs.toml` omits them
  (`line_width` is the one this sprint needs).

document type. `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` Change Guidance
forbids a dependency from the module onto any profile.

Keep the surface minimal. Element records, required sections, reference
properties and lifecycle rules are later features; widening the interface for
a framework-specific reason is explicitly called out as a smell in
`specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md`.

title: Define the SpecIndex index model in Strata
description:
# Define the SpecIndex index model in Strata

**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **IDX**, section "`SpecIndex` index model in Strata (added)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

The CLI emits an index (`specs.json`) that has no data model. The Strata
sources under `schemas/` cover frontmatter, configuration and profile
registration, but not the artifact the CLI *writes*. Because the index
crosses a boundary (the Architecture Catalogue) and must carry a versioned
schema, its shape is defined once in Strata and generated into the same
JSON-Schema/Go/Markdown outputs as every other model, per [[adr-016]].

The model is deliberately **additive**: it holds only the frontmatter-and-path
entries and exclusions this sprint populates, leaving room for later features
to add headings and references under the same `schema_version`.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.


## Design

Add a new Strata source under `schemas/` (e.g. `index.strata`) declaring:

- a root struct carrying `schema_version` (String), `workspace` (String), a
  list of document entries and a list of exclusions;
- a document-entry struct carrying the repository-relative `path` (String),
  the parsed `frontmatter` (the existing `DocumentFrontmatter` envelope or
  per-type struct), and an optional `parse_error` with its position, for a
  member that failed to parse;
- an exclusion struct carrying `path`, a `reason` enum
  (`no-frontmatter` | `unknown-type`), and the declared `type` value where
  the reason is `unknown-type`.

`schema_version` is a required property whose value this sprint fixes at
`"1.0"`. Entries and exclusions are lists whose element order the emitter
controls, so the CO/CACHE deltas can make output deterministic without a
model change.

Anchors: `schemas/*.strata`, `schemas/strata.config.json`,
`scripts/generate-schemas.sh` (regenerates `cli/core/specmodel/`,
`cli/core/schema/`, and the plugin markdown). The generated Go structs land
in the existing `cli/core/specmodel` package the Corpus emitter consumes.

Do not promote the index to a contract document — the blueprint defers that
to `agent-plugins-h6c`, to land with the first consumer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Strata source under `schemas/` declares the index root, the document
      entry and the exclusion struct as described.
- [ ] `schema_version` is a required property fixed at `"1.0"`
      (**proves AC-SPEC-002.2**, unit).
- [ ] Generated artifacts are regenerated and committed, and
      `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` passes.
- [ ] The generated `specmodel.SpecIndex` Go type is usable by the Corpus
      emitter (compiles, fields reachable).
- [ ] Unit tests cover the model's declared shape and version constant, and
      cite AC-SPEC-002.2. Tests cite the ACs they verify with an `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y` comment on the line immediately preceding the test declaration, per `specs/standards/testing-standards.md`.
- [ ] The `SpecIndex` index model is recorded in
      `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` (its Corpus "index model"
      vocabulary), delivered in this same change.

## Retro

### Approach taken

Bootstrapped the Go module at `cli/go.mod`
(`github.com/brettcallaghan/agent-plugins/cli`, `go 1.24`) first, since no
`go.mod` existed anywhere in the repository. Added one new Strata source,
`schemas/index.strata`, declaring `Span`, `ParseError`, `ExclusionReason`,
`IndexEntry`, `IndexExclusion` and `SpecIndex`; regenerated with
`scripts/generate-schemas.sh` and committed the JSON Schema, Go and Markdown
outputs. Added a hand-written sibling package `cli/core/specindex` holding the
`SchemaVersion` constant and a `New(workspace)` constructor, with the model's
unit tests beside it. Recorded the index model in the Corpus component of
`specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`.

### Implicit decisions

- **`Span` and `ParseError` are declared in Strata, in this bead.** The design
  requires "an optional `parse_error` with its position" and the FRD defines a
  position as a `Span`, so the model cannot be expressed without one. Declaring
  it here also means the FIND delta (bge.4), whose `Finding` carries a `Span`,
  inherits it rather than inventing a second one.
- **One new file, `schemas/index.strata`, holds all six declarations** rather
  than splitting `Span` into its own source. All `schemas/*.strata` compile as
  one package and the Go target emits one file, so the split would be cosmetic;
  the bead asked for "a new Strata source", singular.
- **Column is defined as a one-based Unicode codepoint offset, not bytes.**
  The FRD fixes byte offset/length as authoritative and calls line/column
  "readability"; the repo's own `line_width` convention measures codepoints
  rather than bytes, so columns follow it. Documented in the `Span` doc block.
- **`IndexEntry.frontmatter` is optional.** The design reads as if `frontmatter`
  is required and `parse_error` optional, but a member that failed to parse has
  no envelope to carry. Made both optional and documented the invariant:
  exactly one is present.
- **`schema_version` is pinned with the regex `^1\.0$`,** not merely typed as a
  String. That is the strongest expression Strata offers of "fixed at 1.0" and
  it makes the AC-SPEC-002.2 unit test check the schema rather than restate it.
- **The root's list property is named `entries`,** matching the blueprint's
  "entries and exclusions SHALL be lists" wording.
- **`IndexExclusion.type` keeps the wire key `type`,** because AC-SPEC-001.4's
  example shows `"type": "rfc"` in the emitted index.
- **The schema-version constant lives in a new package `cli/core/specindex`,**
  not beside the generated structs: `generate-schemas.sh` does `rm -rf` on
  `cli/core/specmodel/` before every copy, so a hand-written file there — test
  or not — is deleted on the next regeneration. Filed as a discovered item.
- **`New()` initialises both collections to empty slices** so an empty index
  marshals `[]` rather than `null`, which the CACHE delta's byte-identical
  output requirement will need.
- **Also touched `schemas/README.md`** (added the `index.strata` row to its
  source table) and `module-document-core.md`'s `related` + Key Decisions
  (added `adr-016`, which the new text cites). Both are consequences of the
  change rather than separate work.

### Differences from the instructions

- The bead's own AC set was satisfiable as written; nothing was skipped.
- `scripts/check-skills.sh` went from 1 warning to 2 errors on first
  regeneration, because a backticked `` `specs.json` `` inside a Strata doc
  block reaches the generated Markdown, which `check-skills.sh` does not treat
  as generated. Worked around by writing the filename in bold. Filed.

### Surprising / worth improving

- A `@discriminator("type")` union over the per-type frontmatter structs is
  impossible — strata rejects it with "Variant 'Adr' may not override the
  discriminator property 'type'" — so the entry carries the shared
  `DocumentFrontmatter` envelope and per-type properties are not representable.
  `struct Adr: DocumentFrontmatter {}` is empty, which is why AC-SPEC-002.1's
  own example happens to fit. Filed as bearing on bge.8.
- `testing-standards.md` requires unit tests to sit beside their subject, and
  the generation script makes that impossible for exactly the models this bead
  adds. The two rules collide with no guidance on which yields.

title: triage-rfc: check a proposal's extent and sufficiency before adopting (RFC P1)
description:
## Problem

The `triage-rfc` skill verifies that an RFC's quoted evidence EXISTS in
the tree, but never that the evidence is COMPLETE, nor that the proposed
change covers the evidence it cites. Every existing check points at
existence only:

- `.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:270` anti-pattern row: "Adopting
  on plausibility without verifying the quoted evidence" — checks the
  quote is really there.
- `SKILL.md:111` adopt-now criteria: "concrete change, verbatim
  evidence, small blast radius" — none is an extent check.
- `SKILL.md:221` verify bullet: "Re-read each file you changed" —
  scoped to files that DID change, so a file that should have changed
  and did not is outside it by construction.

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Observed in the triage run of 2026-08-01, model claude-opus-5.

EXTENT. RFC 0007 P1 cited four occurrences of retired `@` notation in
three templates. The real count was six in five files:

    $ grep -rn '@<' plugin/skills/
    .../module-blueprint-template.md:317
    .../container-blueprint-template.md:323
    .../component-blueprint-template.md:193
    .../contract-template.md:108
    .../contract-template.md:202
    .../system-blueprint-template.md:219

`component-blueprint-template.md:193` and
`system-blueprint-template.md:219` were never cited — the authoring run
that produced the RFC never opened those two files. The sweep happened
only because that RFC's author wrote "Triage should also sweep the
remaining templates" into the proposal body. Nothing in the skill asks
for it. Adopting P1 as cited would have left two templates emitting
prohibited syntax while the Resolution recorded the class as fixed —
the exact outcome `SKILL.md:223` warns against ("A half-applied
adoption is worse than a deferral, because the Resolution will claim it
landed").

SUFFICIENCY. RFC 0007 P2's proposed text told the reader to assign "a
jsdom `window` and `document` onto `globalThis`". That same RFC's
finding 2 states six globals were needed: `window`, `document`,
`navigator`, `Element`, `HTMLElement`, `SVGElement`. The proposed fix
was inconsistent with the evidence in its own document; adopting it
verbatim would have shipped guidance that still fails.

Source: rfcs/inbox/triage-rfc/rfc-self-triage-rfc-evidence-completeness.md,
proposal P1 (severity blocker, origin self, runs_observed 1).
design:
Insert after step 3's classification list (after the
`already-implemented` bullet, before the line `4. **Present the
recommendation and STOP for approval.**`), at 3-space indent to match
the surrounding step body:

   Before classifying a proposal **adopt-now**, run two checks its
   author could not have run. Both are triage's, and each has a
   recorded outcome:

   - **Extent.** WHEN the evidence cites occurrences of a repeatable
     pattern — a syntax, a phrase, a defect class — enumerate that
     pattern across the whole surface before adopting. A cited list is
     a sample from one run's path, not a census: the reporting run only
     opened the files its task required. Put the enumerating command
     and its result in the Resolution.
   - **Sufficiency.** Read the proposed Change against the finding it
     cites. WHEN the change resolves less than its own evidence
     describes, widen it and adopt with refinement.

   Failing either check does not sink a proposal — it resizes it. A
   proposal whose extent was understated is adopted with refinement
   over the full set, not rejected.

Then append this row to the Anti-Patterns table at the end of the file
(table cells are exempt from the 80-column rule):

| Treating a proposal's cited occurrences as the complete set | The RFC lists what its run touched; a defect class usually reaches files that run never opened, and the Resolution then records as fixed a class that is still live |

Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead — agent-plugins bead for P5
owns the single 1.3 -> 1.4 bump and is last in this chain.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Step 3 carries an Extent check and a Sufficiency check, inserted after the already-implemented bullet
- [ ] The Anti-Patterns table has a row about treating cited occurrences as the complete set
- [ ] Every line added outside a table row is at most 80 characters
- [ ] The skill frontmatter version is NOT changed by this bead
notes: Tier: standard. tier_reason: the wording is supplied verbatim, but it lands in two separate regions of the file (step 3 body and the trailing table) and the table row must be recognised as width-exempt while the prose is not. No C4 component is affected; this file is a skill, not a documented container or module.
close_reason: Step 3 gained Extent and Sufficiency checks; Anti-Patterns gained the cited-occurrences row. Version bump left to agent-plugins-905 per the chain.

title: ADR: index cache invalidation
description:
Requested directly by the user, 2026-07-31: 'ADR the cache invalidation'.

FRD-spec-validation-cli defines a 'warm index' (a cached index whose inputs are unchanged since it was built) and hangs three latency ACs on it — AC-SPEC-009.1, AC-SPEC-009.2 and AC-SPEC-009.4 all assume warmth. Nothing decides how warmth is determined or invalidated.

Open questions the ADR must answer: what keys the cache (content hash, mtime, size, git object id); whether configuration changes invalidate the whole cache or a subset; whether the profile version participates in the key (it must, or a rule change silently reuses stale findings); where the cache lives and whether it is gitignored; what happens on a partial invalidation.
acceptance_criteria: An approved ADR fixing the cache key, the invalidation triggers, the on-disk location, and the correctness argument that a stale finding cannot survive a rule change
close_reason: Decided: content hash (input_hash), not mtime. Recorded on the issue and in the retired blueprint's Tracker Reconciliation; ADR deliberately not authored per the blueprint's stated default.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Superseded by feature-spec-validation-cli: cache staleness is detected by **content hash** of the index's inputs, not mtime — pinned in the CACHE delta of the approved feature blueprint. Close by recording that decision, or write it up as an ADR documenting the rejected mtime alternative (maintainer's choice). Close or re-scope when agent-plugins-bge.16 lands.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
Resolved by feature-spec-validation-cli and closed at its retirement (agent-plugins-bge.16), taking the closing default the blueprint offers rather than authoring the ADR.

DECISION: index cache staleness is detected by a **content hash of the corpus inputs**, not by modification time. The built index carries the digest as input_hash (a sha256: value, visible in 'spec index --out -'); a query or single-document check answers from the persisted specs.json when that digest is unchanged and rebuilds otherwise. Implemented in cli/core/corpus (cache path), verified by cli/core/corpus/cache_test.go citing AC-SPEC-009.1, AC-SPEC-009.2, AC-SPEC-010.5 and AC-SPEC-010.6.

WHY NOT AN ADR: the blueprint offered either closing with the choice recorded or writing it up to document the rejected mtime alternative. Closing is the better fit — mtime was the only alternative in contention and it is not a live trade-off but a defect: a fresh CI checkout carries new mtimes over identical content, so an mtime cache would cold-build on every CI run and defeat the REQ-SPEC-009.1 budget this decision exists to protect. An ADR recording one rejected option with no standing tension would be ceremony. If a second invalidation strategy is ever proposed (e.g. a partial or per-file cache), that is the moment to author one.

title: ADR: adopt strata as the single source of truth for schemas and generated types
description:
Requested in PR #4 review of container-spec-cli (2026-07-31): 'Use strata: git@github.com:strata-lang/strata.git'.

Strata models a structure once and generates JSON Schema, Markdown documentation, and Go structs from that one definition. The reviewer wants it used to model: the specs.toml configuration, the frontmatter structure, the JSON artifacts the tool emits, and the structure of errors/findings emitted as JSON.

## Session setup requirement

This session could NOT reach the strata repo. add_repo failed ('cross-tier adds are not supported in v1'), git clone failed on proxy auth, GitHub MCP is scoped to brettcallaghan/agent-plugins, and WebFetch of raw content 404d. list_repos confirmed the repo IS available to the account (private, can_push).

**Create the next session with BOTH brettcallaghan/agent-plugins AND strata-lang/strata as initial sources.** Without that the ADR cannot be written against the real tool.

## Reading list (from the strata repo root)
- docs/public/strata.llm.md
- docs/content/docs/lang.mdx

## Known constraints
- Do not use the binary from the last release; build the CLI from source (Rust). This is a temporary Rust build-time dependency in a Go project, which the ADR must address.
- Known issue: strata-generated Go structs carry no YAML or TOML tags. The agreed workaround is to convert YAML/TOML to JSON and deserialize from JSON. module-document-core's Frontmatter component already documents this two-step model.
- Strata is a build-time tool whose generated artifacts get committed; advised against embedding strata binaries in this repo (423 KiB packed, distributed by clone via .claude-plugin/marketplace.json).
- Does NOT replace santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema — strata generates the schema, that library validates against it.
acceptance_criteria: An approved ADR recording the strata adoption decision, what it generates, where generated artifacts live and how they are regenerated, how the Rust build-time dependency is managed in CI, and the YAML/TOML tag workaround
